semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا وَقَعَتِ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is a pure adverb (ẓarf) without any conditional meaning, and what governs it is «ليس». The second: what governs it is an implied «اذْكُر» (remember). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: by what is «إذا» put in the accusative? I say: by «ليس», as in your saying «يومَ الجمعة ليس لي شُغْلٌ» (on Friday I have no business)." Then he said: "Or by an implied «اذكُرْ»." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "No grammarian would say this, nor anyone who has picked up anything of the craft of grammar." He said: "Because «لَيْسَ» is like the negating «ما»: there is no event (ḥadath) in it, so how can it govern an adverb without an event? Calling it a verb is figurative, for the definition of the verb does not apply to it." And al-Shaykh said much against him along these lines. Then he said: "As for the example he cited as a parallel, the adverb is not governed by «ليس» but by the khabar (predicate), and something governed by its khabar has been placed before it, which is a disputed question." End of quotation. I say: adverbs are governed by mere traces (rawāʾiḥ) of verbs. The meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that the negation understood from «ليس» is what governs «إذا», as if it were said: "the falsity of its occurrence is negated when it occurs". What I have said is indicated by the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "The second: [it is] an adverb for what is indicated by {لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ}, i.e. when it occurs, it will not prove false." If it is said: then let that be permissible with the negating «ما» as well — the answer is that the verb is closer to indicating an event than the particle.
The third: it is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb) is implied, i.e. "when it occurs, such-and-such will be", and that is what governs it. The fourth: it is conditional, and what governs it is the verb that comes after it and follows it immediately; this is the choice of al-Shaykh, and in it he followed Makkī. Makkī said: "What governs it is «وَقَعَتْ», because it may be used for conditional requital (yujāzā bihā), so the verb after it governs it, just as it governs the conditional «ما» and «مَنْ» in your saying «ما تفعَلُ أفعَلْ» (whatever you do, I will do) and «مَنْ تُكرِمْ أُكْرِمْ» (whomever you honour, I will honour)"; then he mentioned much discussion. The fifth: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «إذا رُجَّتْ» is its khabar (predicate); this is on our view that it is declinable (tataṣarraf), and the discussion of this has already been set out precisely. However, this view was only allowed by al-Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik, Ibn Jinnī and Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī on the reading of whoever put «خافضةً رافعةً» in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Some reported it from al-Akhfash, and I do not know why that is restricted to the accusative reading. [Translator's note: the printed text has «يوجه النصب»; read as «بوجه النصب».]
The sixth: it is an adverb for «خافضة» or «رافعة»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, i.e. "when it occurs it will lower and raise". The seventh: it is an adverb for «رُجَّتْ», and the second «إذا» is, on this view, either a badal (substitute) from the first or a repetition of it. The eighth: what governs it is what is indicated by His saying: {فأصحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ}, i.e. when it occurs, the states of people in it become clear. [Translator's note: the text has «باتَتْ»; perhaps «بانَتْ» (became clear) is intended, and it is translated so.]
The ninth: the apodosis of the condition is His saying {فأصحابُ المَيْمنةِ} to the end.
And «لِوَقْعَتِها» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «كاذبة» is the postponed noun (ism). «كاذبة» may be an active participle — and this is the apparent view — being an adjective of an omitted noun. Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as: "a lying soul, i.e. on that day no one will lie against Allah, and no one will deny the Day of Resurrection." Then he said: "And the lām is like the one in His saying {قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي} [al-Fajr: 24], since it will have no soul that denies it and says to it 'you were not', just as today it has many souls that deny it, saying to it 'you were not'. Or it is from their saying «كَذَّبَتْ فلاناً نفسُه» in a great danger, when his soul encourages him to undertake it and says to him: 'you can bear it and more than it, so face it and do not mind it' — in the sense that it is an event that cannot be borne for its severity and horror, and that no soul will at that time tell its owner what it tells him in the face of momentous matters, making it seem attractive to him to endure and bear it; because on that day they will be weaker and more abject than that. Do you not see His saying {كالفراش المبثوث} [al-Qāriʿa: 4]? And moths are proverbial for weakness." Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplied it as: "a lying state". He said: "On this view the speech admits two meanings. The first: lying, i.e. lied about in what was reported about it, so He called it lying for this reason, as you say: 'this is a lying story', i.e. lied about. The second: i.e. its occurrence will not fail to come about, as in your saying: 'so-and-so, when he attacks, does not falter.'" [The second view:] that «كاذبة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of denial (takdhīb), like «خائنة الأعين». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From your saying «حَمَلَ فلانٌ على قرْنِه فما كَذَبَ», i.e. he did not turn coward or hold back; its literal meaning is that he did not belie what his soul told him about his ability to face him and his daring against him." And he cited for Zuhayr:
4200 - لَيْثٌ بعَثَّرَ يَصْطادُ الرجالُ إذا ... ما الليثُ كَذَّب عن أقرانِه صَدَقا (A lion at ʿAththar that hunts men; when the lion holds back from its opponents, he holds true.)
"i.e. when it occurs, it will have no turning back and no retreat." End of quotation. This is very good speech.
Then you have two views on this clause. The first: it has no grammatical position, either because it is an initial (ibtidāʾiyya) clause — especially on al-Zamakhsharī's view, since he made the adverb attached to it — or because it is parenthetical between the condition and its omitted apodosis. The second: its position is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, and did not explain what the owner of the ḥāl is; it is clear, since there is nothing here but «الواقعة», and Abū al-Faḍl stated this explicitly.
The majority read «خافضةٌ رافعةٌ» in the nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is lowering one people into the Fire and raising others into Paradise"; the object is omitted because the meaning is understood. Or the meaning is: it is characterised by lowering and raising, as in His saying {يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 156] and {وكُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 187]. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Miqsam and al-Yazīdī read them in the accusative as ḥāls. It is reported that al-Kisāʾī said: "Had al-Yazīdī not preceded me in it, I would have read it so." End of quotation. I do not think that such a thing is authentic from such a man.
There is disagreement about the owner of the ḥāl. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "From the pronoun in «كاذبة» or in «وَقَعَتْ»"; its correction would be to say: "or the agent of «وقعَتْ»", since there is no [latent] pronoun in «وقعَتْ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Faḍl said: from «الواقعة»; then they established that multiple ḥāls can come from a single owner, just as multiple predicates can come. I have explained this to you earlier, so I can dispense with their discussion. Abū al-Faḍl said: "If all of these are made ḥāls, what governs «إذا وَقَعَتْ» is omitted, indicated by the import [of the passage], i.e. when it occurs they will be brought to account."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {والسابقون السابقون}: there are several views on it. The first: they are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). There are two interpretations of this. The first: it means "the forerunners — they are those whose state is well known for that", like their saying «أنت أنت» (you are [truly] you) and «والناسُ الناسُ», and his saying:
4201 - أنا أبو النجمِ وشِعْري شِعْري ... (I am Abū al-Najm, and my poetry is [still] my poetry.) This is said in magnifying and exalting a matter, and it is the doctrine of Sībawayh.
The second interpretation: what the two acts of preceding are attached to is different, since the implied form is: "those who are foremost to faith are those foremost to Paradise", or "those foremost to obedience to Allah are those foremost to His mercy", or "those foremost to good are those foremost to Paradise".
The second view: that the second «السابقون» is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, and «أولئك المقرَّبون» is a nominal clause in the position of the khabar of the first, the linking element (rābiṭ) being the demonstrative, as in His saying: {وَلِبَاسُ التقوى ذلك خَيْرٌ} [al-Aʿrāf: 26] in the reading of whoever read «لباسُ» in the nominative, on one of the views.
The third: that [the second] «السابقون» is an adjective (naʿt) of the first, the khabar being the aforementioned clause. This should not be given any attention: how can a thing be described with its own wording, and what benefit is there in that? The most likely to me, if this expression has come from someone who is taken into account, is that he called the tawkīd an adjective; Sībawayh did something close to this.
The fourth: that one pauses at His saying «والسابقون», and His saying «السابقون، أولئك المقرَّبون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar. This requires that «والسابقون» be conjoined to what precedes it; but its conjunction to what immediately precedes it is not fitting; it is only fitting to conjoin it to «أصحابُ المَيْمنة», as if it were said: "and the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right! — and the foremost", i.e. what are the foremost!, magnifying them, so that they share with the companions of the right in the magnification. On this view His saying «وأصحابُ المَشْأمَةِ، ما أصحابُ المشأمة» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items. There is very great strain in this view.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {ثُلَّةٌ}: the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are". It may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, i.e. "of them is a multitude", i.e. of the foremost, meaning that the division applies to the foremost. Or it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is {فِي جَنَّاتِ النعيم} or His saying «على سُرُر». So these are four views.
Al-thulla is a group of people. Al-Zamakhsharī restricted it to a large one, and cited:
4202 - وجاءَتْ إليهم ثُلَّةٌ خِنْدِفِيَّةٌ ... بجيشٍ كتَيَّارٍ مِنْ البحرِ مُزْبِدِ (A company of Khindif came against them with an army like a foaming torrent of the sea.)
No one else restricted it; rather, they stated explicitly that it is a group, few or many. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-thulla is a gathered piece of wool, and for that reason sheep were called thalla." I say: he means with fatḥa on the thāʾ; from it is his saying:
4203 - أَمْرَعَتِ الأرضُ لَوَ أنَّ مالا ... لَوْ أن نُوْقاً لك أو جِمالا
أو ثَلَّةً مِنْ غنم إمَّا لا ...
(The land has become fertile — if only there were wealth, if only you had she-camels or he-camels, or a flock of sheep, if nothing else.)
End of quotation. Then al-Rāghib said: "Considering the notion of gathering it was said: «ثُلَّة من الأوَّلين، وثُلَّة من الآخِرين», i.e. a group. «ثَلَّلْتُ كذا»: I took a portion of it. «ثَلَّ عرشَه»: he brought down a part of it. Al-thalal is shortness of the teeth through the falling out of some of them. «أثَلَّ فَمُه»: his teeth fell out. «تَثَلَّلَتِ الرَّكِيَّةُ»: the well collapsed." End of quotation. So he stated without qualification that it is a group, without restriction to few or many; the largeness that al-Zamakhsharī understood may come from the context. And «مِنْ الأوَّلِين» is an adjective of «ثُلَّة», and likewise «مِنْ الآخِرين» is an adjective of «قليل».

semin-durr:15-15.t:
Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Abū al-Sammāl read «سُرَر» with fatḥa on the first rāʾ; it has been mentioned before that this is a dialectal form of some of Kalb and Tamīm. Al-mawḍūna is the woven; its origin is from «وضَنْتُ الشيءَ», i.e. I set one part of it upon another. From it the coat of mail was called mawḍūna, because of the overlapping of its rings. Al-Aʿshā said:
4204 - ومِن نَسْجِ داودَ مَوْضَوْنَةً ... تسيرُ مع الحيِّ عِيْراً فَعِيْرا (And of the weaving of David, a close-woven [mail] that travels with the tribe, caravan after caravan.)
From it also is «وَضِين الناقة», which is its girth, because of the overlapping of its strands. The rajaz poet said:
4205 - إليك تَعْدُو قِلقاً وضِيْنُها ... مُعْتَرضاً في بَطْنِها جنينُها
مُخالفاً دينَ النَّصارى دينُها ...
(To You she runs, her girth loose, her foetus lying crosswise in her belly, her religion opposed to the religion of the Christians.)
Al-Rāghib said: "Al-waḍn is the weaving of the coat of mail, and it is borrowed for every firm weaving", so he made it originally [refer] to the weaving of mail. The poet said:
4206 - تقولُ وقد دَرَأْتُ لها وَضِيْني ... أهذا دينُه أبداً ودِيني (She says, when I loosened my girth for her: is this forever his habit and mine?)
i.e. my girth.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {مُّتَّكِئِينَ، مُتَقَابِلِينَ}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun in «على سُرُر». It may also be an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila), so that «متقابلين» is a ḥāl from the pronoun of «متَّكئين».

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {يَطُوفُ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it may be resumptive (istiʾnāf).

semin-durr:18-18.t:
And «بأكْواب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَطُوف». Al-abārīq is the plural of «إبْريق», which is one of the vessels for wine. He said:
4207 - أَفْنى تِلادي وما جَمَّعْتُ مِنْ نَشَبٍ ... قَرْعُ القواقيزِ أَفْواهَ الأباريقِ (My inherited wealth and the property I gathered have been used up by the cups knocking against the mouths of the ewers.)
ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
4208 - وتداعَوا إلى الصَّبوحِ فجاءتْ ... قَيْنةٌ في يمينِها إبْريقُ (They called one another to the morning draught, and a singing-girl came with a ewer in her right hand.)
Another said: 4209 - كأن إبْريقَهم ظبيٌ على شَرَفٍ ... مُفَدَّمٍ بسَبا الكَتَّانِ مَلْثُوْمُ (As if their ewer were a gazelle on a height, its mouth stopped with a linen strainer, veiled.)
Its pattern is ifʿīl, since it is derived from «البَريق» (gleam). The ibrīq is one that has a spout; some said: and a handle. The explanation of «الأكواب» has been given before.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يُصَدَّعُونَ}: it may be resumptive, reporting this about them, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم». The meaning of «لا يُصَدَّعون عنها» is: because of it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its literal meaning is: their headache does not proceed from it." Al-ṣudāʿ is the well-known ailment that afflicts a person in his head, and wine affects it. ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada said, describing wine:
4210 - تَشْفي الصُّداعَ ولا يُؤْذِيك صالبُها ... ولا يخالِطُها في الرأس تدويمُ (It cures the headache, its fever does not harm you, and no dizziness mixes with it in the head.)
When I read this dīwān with al-Shaykh Athīr al-Dīn Abū Ḥayyān, may Allah have mercy on him, he said to me: "This is the description of the wine of Paradise." And he said to me: "When I read it with al-Shaykh Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, he said to me: 'This is the description of the wine of Paradise.'" It has also been said: «لا يُصَدَّعون»: they are not separated, as drinkers disperse from drinking because of worldly occurrences. Among instances of «تَصَدَّعَ» in the sense of «تَفَرَّق» is his saying «فتصدَّع السحابُ عن المدينة» (the clouds parted from Medina), i.e. dispersed. This is supported by the reading of Mujāhid «لا يَصَّدَّعون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and a doubled ṣād; the original is «يَتَصَدَّعون», i.e. they disperse, as in His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ} [al-Rūm: 43]. Al-Zamakhsharī reported a reading «لا يُصَدِّعون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the ṣād light, and kasra on the doubled dāl; he said: i.e. they do not separate one another, i.e. they do not disperse them. The disagreement among the Seven over «يُنزِفُونَ» and its explanation have been given before.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy, from «نَزَفَ البِئْرُ», i.e. what was in it was drawn out; the meaning is: their wine will not run out. Al-Shaykh said: "Ibn Abī Isḥāq also, and ʿAbd Allāh, al-Jaḥdarī, al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā, [read] with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy, i.e. their drink does not run out." I say: this is astonishing from him, for it has been mentioned in al-Ṣāffāt that the Kufans read in al-Wāqiʿa with kasra on the zāy, and he himself transmitted this reading in his poem.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {وَفَاكِهَةٍ}: the majority read «فاكهة» and «لحم» in the genitive, conjoined to «أكواب», i.e. they go round among them with these things: what is eaten, what is drunk, and what is enjoyed as a delicacy; and this is the perfection of a pleasant life. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read both in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being implied, i.e. "and they will have such-and-such".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {إِذَا رُجَّتِ}: it may be a badal (substitute) from the first «إذا», or a tawkīd (emphasis) of it, or its khabar (predicate) on the view that the first is a mubtadaʾ (subject), as all of this has been set out precisely before. It may also be conditional, and what governs it is either implied or its verb that follows it, as was said about its counterpart. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be put in the accusative by «خافضة رافعة», i.e. it lowers and raises at the time of the shaking of the earth and the crumbling of the mountains, because at that time what is high is lowered and what is low is raised." Al-Shaykh said: "It is not permissible for it to be put in the accusative by both together, but only by one of them, because two effective causes do not combine on a single effect." I say: the meaning of his words is that each of the two has a hold on it in terms of meaning, and the question is one of contention (tanāzuʿ, two governors competing for one word); then the expression is correct, since it is true that each of the two governs it, even if in alternation.
Al-rajj is violent shaking, in the sense of «زُلزلت» (was quaked). «وبُسَّت الجبالُ»: [the mountains] were made to move, from their saying «بَسَّ الغنمَ», i.e. he drove them; or in the sense of "were crumbled", as in His saying: {يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفاً} [Ṭāhā: 105]; this is indicated by {فَكَانَتْ هَبَآءً مُّنبَثّاً}. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «رَجَّتْ» and «بَسِّتْ» in the active voice, on the view that «رجَّ» and «بَسَّ» are both intransitive and transitive, i.e. it was removed and went away. [Translator's note: the printed «بَسِّتْ» presumably stands for «بَسَّتْ».] Al-Nakhaʿī read «مْنْبَتَّاً» with two dots above, i.e. cut off, from «البَتّ»; the meaning of the verse is averse to it.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فَأَصْحَابُ الميمنة مَآ أَصْحَابُ الميمنة}: the first «أصحاب» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is an interrogative expressing magnification, a second mubtadaʾ; the second «أصحاب» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of the first. The repetition of the mubtadaʾ here in its own wording dispenses with the [resumptive] pronoun; similar to it are {الحاقة مَا الحآقة} [al-Ḥāqqa: 1-2] and {القارعة مَا القارعة} [al-Qāriʿa: 1-2], and that only occurs in contexts of magnification. Here there is a question: «ما» is indefinite and what comes after it is definite, so it should have been said that «ما» is a fronted khabar and the second «أصحاب» and the like is the mubtadaʾ, since the definite noun is more entitled to be a mubtadaʾ than the indefinite. This question is raised against Sībawayh in the like of this, and in your saying «كم مالُك» (how much is your wealth?) and «مَرَرْتُ برجل خيرٌ منه أبوه» (I passed by a man whose father is better than he), for he parses the interrogative «ما», «كم» and «أَفْعَل» as mubtadaʾ and what comes after them as their khabar. The answer: the indefinite noun's occurring as a predicate of these things became exceedingly common, so the category was made uniform to run on a single course. Thus they answered; but this is not strong enough to prevent «ما», «كم» and afʿal from being a fronted khabar. Had this been said, it would not be a mistake; rather, it is closer to being correct.
Al-maymana is [on the pattern] mafʿala from the root of «اليُمْن» (good fortune); likewise al-mashʾama is from «اليد الشُّؤمى», which is the left hand, because the Arabs took it as an ill omen; or from «الشُّؤْم» (ill omen).

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَحُورٌ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «حور عين» in the genitive, and the rest read both in the nominative. Al-Nakhaʿī [read] «وحِيرٍ عين», changing the wāw into a yāʾ, with both in the genitive; and Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh [read] «حُوْراً عيناً», with both in the accusative. As for the genitive, it is from several views. The first: it is conjoined to {جَنَّاتِ النعيم} [al-Wāqiʿa: 12], as if it were said: they are in gardens, and fruit, and meat, and houris; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Al-Shaykh said: "This is far-fetched, and a breaking apart of speech whose parts are bound to one another; it is a foreigner's understanding." I say: what he went for is a very fine meaning, and it is on the omission of a muḍāf (first term of an annexation), i.e. "and in the nearness of houris"; this is what al-Zamakhsharī meant, and others have stated this muḍāf explicitly. The second: it is conjoined to «بأكواب», and that is by taking His saying «يطُوفُ» loosely, since its meaning is: they are given delight in it with cups, and with such-and-such, and with houris; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The third: it is conjoined to it in reality, and the youths go round among them with the houris too, since there is pleasure for them in that; they go round among them with what is eaten, drunk and enjoyed as a delicacy, after [bringing] the one wedded. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and Quṭrub held this view. No attention is to be paid to the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "conjoined to «أكواب» in wording but not in meaning, because the houris are not carried around."
As for the nominative, it is also from several views. [The first:] conjoined to «ولْدانٌ», i.e. the houris go round among them with that, as servant-girls do in this world. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. they go round among them for enjoyment, not for service." I say: it is more eloquent [taken] as service, because if the like of those serve them, then what do you think of those who are wedded? The second: that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun concealed in «مُتَّكِئين», this being made permissible by the separation [by the words] between them. The third: that it is conjoined to a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) both omitted, its implied form being: "they have all this, and wide-eyed houris"; al-Shaykh said this. It is open to objection (fīhi naẓar), because it is only conjoined to the mubtadaʾ alone, and that khabar belongs to it and to what it is conjoined to.
The fourth: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, its implied form being: "and they have", or "in it are", or "there are" houris. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "On [the implied form] 'and in it are houris', like the verse of al-Kitāb [of Sībawayh]:
4211 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إلاَّ رَواكدَ جَمْرُهُنَّ هَباءُ (… except for the still [hearth-stones], whose embers are dust.)"
The fifth: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "their women are houris"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. As for the accusative, there are two views on it. The first: it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "they are given" or "they inherit" houris. The second: it is construed according to the meaning of «يَطوف عليهم», because its meaning is "they are given such-and-such", so this was conjoined to it. Makkī said: "The accusative is also permissible, by construing it according to the meaning; because the meaning of 'youths go round with such-and-such' is 'they are given such-and-such', then «حوراً» is conjoined to its meaning" — as if he had not come across it as a reading.
As for the reading «وحِيْرٍ», it is because of its adjacency to «عين», and because the yāʾ is lighter than the wāw. Its parallel in alteration for adjacency is «أَخَذَه ما قَدُم وما حَدُث» (he was seized by what is old and what is new), with ḍamma on the dāl of «حَدُث» because of «قَدُم»; when it is used alone you give its dāl fatḥa. And his saying, peace be upon him:
«وربِّ السماوات ومَنْ أَظْلَلْنَ ورَبِّ الشياطين ومَنْ أَضْلَلْنَ» ("Lord of the heavens and what they shade, and Lord of the devils and whom they lead astray"); and his saying, peace be upon him: «أيتكنَّ صاحبةُ الجمل الأَرْبَب تَنْبَحُها كلابُ الحَوْءَب» ("Which of you is the rider of the hairy camel at whom the dogs of al-Ḥawʾab will bark?") — he separated the doubled letter in «الأَرْبَب» because of «الحَوْءَب».
Qatāda read «وحورُ عينٍ» in the nominative, annexed to «عين», and Ibn Miqsam in the accusative with annexation; the justification of the nominative and accusative has been given. As for the annexation, it is a case of annexing the described noun to its adjective, by interpretation. ʿIkrima read «وحَوْراءَ عَيْناءَ» with both in the singular, intending the genus. This reading admits two possibilities: it may be accusative, like the reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh, or genitive, like the reading of the two brothers, because these two nouns are diptotes, so they admit both. The discussion of the derivation of «العِين» has been given before.

semin-durr:23-23.t: And {كَأَمْثَالِ} is an adjective (ṣifa) or a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «جزاءً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense".

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ قِيلاً}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and this is clear, because it is not included under idle talk and sinful speech. The second: it is a joined (muttaṣil) [exception], and this is far-fetched; it is as if this [person] held that the underlying sense is "they will not hear in it any speech", so it was included in it in his view. Makkī said: "It has also been said: it is accusative by «يَسْمعون»", and it seems he meant this view.
His saying: {سَلاَماً سَلاَماً}: there are several views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from «قيلاً», i.e. they will hear in it only "peace, peace". The second: it is an adjective (naʿt) of «قيلاً». The third: it is accusative by «قيلاً» itself, i.e. except that they say "peace, peace"; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb, that verb being reported by «قيلاً», its implied form being: "except a saying: be safe, a safety".
It has also been read «سَلامٌ» in the nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "as a quotation (ḥikāya)". Makkī said: "In speech the nominative is permissible in the sense of 'peace be upon you', a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate)" — as if he did not know it as a reading.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {مَّخْضُودٍ}: al-makhḍūd is that whose thorns have been cut off, from «خَضَدْتُه», i.e. I cut it. It has also been said: the one laden with fruit so that its trunk cannot be seen and its branches bend, from «خَضَدْت الغصنَ», i.e. I bent it. Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt said:
4212 - إن الحَدائقَ في الجِنانِ ظليلةٌ ... فيها الكواعِبُ سِدْرُها مَخْضُوْدُ (The orchards in the gardens are shady; in them are full-breasted maidens, and their lote-trees are thornless.)
Al-ṭalḥ is the plural of «الطلحة», which is the great one among thorny trees; it has also been said: it is the umm ghaylān [acacia]. Mujāhid said: but its fruit is sweeter than honey. It has also been said: it is the banana. The meaning of «مَنْضود» is: layered. In the tafsīr: no trunk can be seen for it because of the abundance of its fruit. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, ʿAbd Allāh and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read «وطَلْع» with ʿayn. When ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read it, he said: "What has the ṭalḥ to do with it?", and cited as evidence His saying: {لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ} [Qāf: 10]. It was said to him: "Shall we change it?" He said: "The verses of the Qurʾān are not to be stirred up today, nor changed." Something similar is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās. «ومَسْكوب»: i.e. poured out in abundance. «فاكهة» has also been read in the nominative, i.e. "and there is", or "they have", or "in it is", or "there is" fruit.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {لاَّ مَقْطُوعَةٍ}: there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is an adjective (naʿt) of «فاكهة», and «لا» is for negation, as in your saying «مَرَرْتُ برجلٍ لا طويلٍ ولا قصير» (I passed by a man neither tall nor short); for that reason its repetition is required. The second: it is conjoined to «فاكهة», and «لا» is a conjunction; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. In that case a described noun must be omitted, i.e. "not fruit that is cut off", so that the adjective is not conjoined to its described noun.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {وَفُرُشٍ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ, plural of «فِراش». Abū Ḥaywa [read] it with a sukūn, a lightened form of the well-known one. Al-furush, it has been said, are the familiar furnishings, raised upon couches. It has also been said: it is a metonymy (kināya) for women, just as they are alluded to by "garment"; Abū ʿUbayda and others said this. They said: for that reason He referred the pronoun to them in His saying «إنَّا أنشأناهنَّ». Others answered: it refers to the women indicated by «الفُرُش». It has also been said: it refers to the previously mentioned «حُور». From al-Akhfash: «هُنَّ» is a pronoun for something not mentioned, i.e. the context indicates it.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {عُرُباً}: plural of «عَروب», like «صَبور» and «صُبُر». Al-ʿarūb is the one who shows love to her husband. It has also been said: the beautiful. It has also been said: the one who speaks well. Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read it with a sukūn on the rāʾ; this is like «رُسُل» and «رُسْل», «فُرُش» and «فُرْش». Ibn ʿAbbās said: "They are the young maidens." And he cited for Labīd:
4213 - وفي الخُدورِ عَروبٌ غيرُ فاحِشةٍ ... رَيَّا الرَّوادِفِ يَعْشى دونَها البصَرُ (And in the curtained litters is a loving woman, not indecent, full-hipped, before whom the eye is dazzled.)
His saying: {أَتْرَاباً}: plural of «تِرْب», which is one who is equal to you in age, because the dust (al-turāb) touches the skin of both at the same time; this is stronger in [making for] affinity. It is one of the nouns that do not become definite by annexation, because it is in the sense of an adjective, since its meaning is "your equal"; similar to it is «خِدْنُك» (your intimate), because it is in the sense of "your companion".

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {لأِّصْحَابِ اليمين}: there are two views on this lām. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ», i.e. "for the sake of". The second: it is attached to «أَتْراباً», as in your saying «هذا تِرْبٌ لهذا», i.e. equal to him.

semin-durr:43-43.t: And al-yaḥmūm: its pattern is fayʿūl. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "From «الحِمَم» or «الحَميم»." Al-yaḥmūm, it has been said, is jet-black smoke. It has also been said: a valley in Hell. It has also been said: one of its names. The first is more apparent.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {لاَّ بَارِدٍ وَلاَ كَرِيمٍ}: two adjectives of «الظلّ», like His saying «من يَحْموم». In this there is the issue that He would have placed the non-explicit [adjective, the prepositional phrase] before the explicit one; so it is better to make it an adjective of «يَحْموم», though the context points to the first.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «لا باردٌ ولا كريمٌ», both in the nominative, i.e. "it is not cool", as in his saying:
4214 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
فأَبِيْتُ لا حَرِجٌ ولا مَحْرومُ (… and I spend the night neither constrained nor deprived.)

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {الحنث}: in the origin of their speech it is the heavy load, and sin and offence were called by it because of their heaviness; al-Khaṭṭābī said this. «فلانٌ حَنَثَ في يمينه»: i.e. he did not fulfil it, because he usually sins [thereby]. Al-ḥinth is used to express reaching puberty; from it is «لم يَبْلُغوا الحنث». That was said only because a person, when he reaches it, is held accountable for al-ḥinth, i.e. for sin. «تَحَنَّثَ فلانٌ»: i.e. he kept away from al-ḥinth. In the hadith: «كان يَتَحَنَّثُ بغار حراء» ("he used to devote himself to worship in the cave of Ḥirāʾ"), i.e. he worshipped, keeping away from sin; like «تَحَرَّجَ»; so tafaʿʿala in all of these is for privation (salb).

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {أَإِذَا مِتْنَا}: the explanation of all this has been given in al-Ṣāffāt, and the discussion of the two interrogatives has been given in Sūrat al-Raʿd; that makes it unnecessary to repeat all of it, and praise be to Allah.

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {مِن شَجَرٍ مِّن زَقُّومٍ}: there are several views on it. The first: the first «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and the second is explicative (bayān), i.e. beginning to eat from trees which are zaqqūm. The second: the second «مِنْ» is an adjective of «شجر», so it is attached to an omitted [word], i.e. "being". The third: the first «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "will surely eat trees", and the second «مِنْ» is according to the two views mentioned about it. The fourth: the reverse of this, namely that the second is redundant, i.e. "will surely eat zaqqūm", and the first «مِنْ» is for beginning, or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «زَقُّوم», i.e. "being from trees"; had it come after, it would have been an adjective. The fifth: «مِنْ شجر» is an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. "will surely eat something of trees", and «ومِنْ زَقُّوم» is, on this view, an adjective of «شجر» or of the omitted «شيء». The sixth: the first is partitive (tabʿīḍ) and the second is a badal (substitute) from it. The pronoun in «منها» refers to «الشجر», and the one in «عليه» also to «الشجر»; it has been mentioned that a generic noun may be masculine or feminine, and that these are two dialectal usages. It has also been said: the one in «عليه» refers to «الزقوم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "to what is eaten". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "to what is eaten or to the eating." End of quotation; there is far-fetchedness in his saying "the eating". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made the pronoun of «الشجر» feminine according to the meaning, and masculine according to the wording in «منها» and «عليه». Whoever read {مِن شَجَرٍ مِّن زَقُّومٍ} made both pronouns refer to the tree, and only made the second masculine by interpreting it as «الزَّقُّوم», since that is its explanation." [Translator's note: the variant reading al-Zamakhsharī refers to is presumably «مِن شَجَرَةٍ مِّن زَقُّومٍ» (singular); the source repeats the wording «مِن شَجَرٍ», which is translated as written.]

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {شُرْبَ الهيم}: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with ḍamma on the shīn, the rest of the Seven with fatḥa, and Mujāhid and Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī with kasra. It has been said: the three are dialectal forms of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «شَرِب», and the one formed by rule among them is only the one with fatḥa. It has also been said: the maṣdar is the one with fatḥa, while those with ḍamma and kasra are two nouns for what is drunk, like «الرِّعْي» (pasture) and «الطِّحْن» (flour). Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «شرِبْتُ شُرباً وشَرْباً». The saying of Jaʿfar is transmitted: «أيامُ مِنى أيامُ أكلٍ وشُرْبٍ وبِعال» ("The days of Minā are days of eating, drinking and conjugal relations") with fatḥa on the shīn. Al-sharb in other than this is a noun for a company of drinkers. He said:
4215 - كأنَّه خارِجٌ من جَنْبِ صَفْحَتِهِ ... سَفُّوْدُ شَرْبٍ نَسُوْهُ عند مُفْتَأَدِ (As if, coming out from the side of its flank, were the roasting-spit of a drinking party who forgot it by the fire-pit.)
The meaning is: like the drinking of al-hīm. As for «الهِيْم», there are several views on it. The first: it is the plural of «أَهْيمَ» or «هَيْماء», which is the he-camel and she-camel afflicted by al-huyām, a disease causing thirst, from which camels drink until they die or fall gravely ill. The original was «هُيْم» with ḍamma on the hāʾ, like «أَحْمر» and «حَمْراء» and «حُمْر»; the ḍamma was changed into a kasra so that the yāʾ remains sound, as in «بِيْض» from «أبيض». A verse of Dhū al-Rumma was cited:
4216 - فأصبَحْتُ كالهَيْماءِ لا الماءُ مُبْرِدٌ ... صَداها ولا يَقْضي عليها هُيامُها (I have become like the thirst-stricken she-camel: water does not cool her thirst, nor does her disease finish her off.)
The second: it is the plural of «هائِم» and «هائِمة», also from al-huyām; except that the plural of fāʿil and fāʿila on fuʿl is rare and uncommon, as in «بازِل» and «بُزْل», «عائِذ» and «عُوْذ»; from it is «العُوْذُ المَطافيل» (the she-camels that have recently given birth, with their young). It has also been said: it is from al-huyām which is going off [aimlessly], because when the camel is afflicted by that, it wanders off at random. The third: it is the plural of «هَيام» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, which is loose sand that is never saturated by water; so it would be like «سَحاب» and «سُحُب» with two ḍammas, then lightened by making its second radical quiescent, then its first radical was given kasra so that the yāʾ remains sound, as was done with the one before it. The fourth: it is the plural of «هُيام» with ḍamma on the hāʾ, which is also loose sand, a dialectal form of «الهَيام» with fatḥa, reported by Thaʿlab, although the well-known form is with fatḥa; then it was made plural on fuʿl, as in «قُراد» and «قُرْد», then lightened and its first radical given kasra so that the yāʾ remains sound. The meaning is: such hunger afflicts them that it drives them to eat the zaqqūm, and such thirst that it compels them to drink the boiling water like the drinking of al-hīm. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how is it correct to conjoin 'drinkers' to 'drinkers', when they are for the same persons and are two matching attributes, so that it would be conjoining a thing to itself? I say: they are not matching, inasmuch as their drinking it, as it is, extreme in heat and cutting the bowels, is a wondrous matter; and their drinking it in that state as the thirsty camels drink is also a wondrous matter; so they are two different attributes." End of quotation. He means His saying: «فشاربون عليه من الحميم، فشاربون». It is a good question, and its answer is like it.
Some answered it with another answer, namely that His saying {فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الهيم} is an explanation of the drinking before it. Do you not see that what precedes it could be like the drinking of al-hīm or like the drinking of others? So He explained it as being like the drinking of these beasts or of the sands.
In that there are two benefits. The first: drawing attention to how much they drink of it. The second: the uselessness of the drinking, and that the drink does them no good, just as it does no good for al-hīm, according to both explanations.
Al-Shaykh said: "The fāʾ requires succession in the two drinkings: first, when they grew thirsty, they drank of the boiling water, thinking it would allay their thirst; the thirst increased through the heat of the boiling water, so they then drank a drinking after which no quenching ever comes, and it is like the drinking of al-hīm. So they are two drinkings of the boiling water, not one drinking whose two attributes differed so that it was conjoined. That which is drunk from in {فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الهيم} is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: 'drinking of it'." End of quotation. The apparent view is that it is one drinking; indeed, this alone is what we hold. How would it be fitting that their increasing in thirst by drinking it should require their drinking of it a second time?

semin-durr:56-56.t:
The majority read «نُزُلُهم» with two ḍammas. It is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr by several routes, and from Nāfiʿ and Ibn Muḥayṣin, with a ḍamma and a sukūn, which is a lightened form. It has been mentioned that al-nuzul is what is prepared for a guest. It has also been said: it is the first thing he eats. So this was called by it in mockery of those for whom it is prepared; in meaning it is like the saying of Abū al-Saʿr al-Ḍabbī:
4217 - وكُنَّا إذا الجبَّارُ أَنْزَلَ جَيْشَه ... جَعَلْنَا القَنا والمُرْهَفاتِ له نُزْلا (Whenever a tyrant brought his army down [on us], we made spears and sharpened blades his hospitality.)

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {فَلَوْلاَ تُصَدِّقُونَ}: an urging (taḥḍīḍ). What the believing is attached to is omitted, its implied form being: "why then do you not believe in Our creating [you]?"

semin-durr:58-58.t: And His saying: {أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ}: it is in the sense of "tell me". Its first object is «ما تُمْنُوْن», and the second is the interrogative clause; the explanation of this has been given before.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
And {أَأَنتُمْ}: two views are possible on it. The first: it is the agent of an implied verb, i.e. "do you create it?"; when the verb was omitted because what follows indicates it, the pronoun became detached; this is of the category of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). The second: «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause after it is its khabar (predicate). The first is preferable because of the interrogative particle.
And His saying: {أَم}: two views are possible on it. The first: it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿa), because a clause comes after it, whereas [the joined one] only conjoins single words. The second: it is joined (muttaṣila). They answered about the clause occurring after it: the predicate after «نحن» was brought by way of emphasis, since had He said «أم نحنُ» that would have sufficed without the predicate. Its parallel is the answer of one asked "[Who] is in the house?": "Zayd is in the house", or "Zayd is in it", whereas had he confined himself to "Zayd" it would have been sufficient. I say: its being joined is supported by the fact that the speech requires its interpretation to be "which of the two matters is the case?"; and if that is valid, it is joined, since the clause is interpreted as a single word.
The object of «الخالقون» is omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e. "the creators of it".
The majority read «تُمْنُوْن» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, from «أَمْنَى يُمْني». Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū al-Sammāl [read] it with fatḥa, from «مَنَى يَمْنِي». Al-Zamakhsharī said: one says «أمْنَى النُّطْفَةَ ومَناها». Allah the Exalted said: {مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تمنى} [al-Najm: 46]. End of quotation. The apparent sense of this is that it is cited as evidence for the triliteral [form], but there is no proof for it in it, since from the quadriliteral one also says «تُمْنَى», as in saying «أنت تُكْرَم» (you are honoured), which is from «أَكْرَم».

semin-durr:60-60.t: Ibn Kathīr read «قَدَرْنا» with the dāl light, and the rest with doubling here; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, in the sense of decreeing, which is ordaining (al-qaḍāʾ).

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {على أَن نُّبَدِّلَ}: it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مَسْبوقين», and this is the apparent view: no one can outstrip Us in Our replacing [you with] your likes, i.e. render Us incapable; one says «سبقَه على كذا», i.e. he made him incapable of it and overcame him in it. The second: it is attached to His saying «قَدَّرنا», i.e. We have decreed among you that We should replace, i.e. cause one group to die and create in its place another group; al-Ṭabarī stated its meaning. On this view His saying {وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ} is parenthetical, and it is a fine parenthesis.
Two views are possible regarding «أمثالَكم». The first: it is the plural of «مِثْل» with kasra on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ, i.e. We are able to annihilate you and create another people like you; this is supported by «إنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكم أيها الناسُ ويَأْتِ بآخرين». The second: it is the plural of «مَثَل» with two fatḥas, which is the attribute, i.e. We change the attributes you have, in physical form and character, and bring you into being in other attributes.

semin-durr:62-62.t: The two readings of «النشأة» have been given in al-ʿAnkabūt.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {أَفَرَأَيْتُم} and what follows it: its parallel has been given before. Here the apodosis of «لو» is brought joined with the lām, and this is more common, because it is affirmative; and it is omitted in His saying «جَعَلْناه أُجاجاً», because the favour in what is eaten is greater than in what is drunk.
Ṭalḥa read «تَذْكُرُون» with sukūn on the dhāl and ḍamma on the kāf.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {فَظَلْتُمْ}: this is the reading of the majority, I mean fatḥa on the ẓāʾ with a single lām; its discussion has been given in full in Ṭāhā. Abū Ḥaywa, and Abū Bakr in one transmission, [read] with kasra on the ẓāʾ. ʿAbd Allāh and al-Jaḥdarī [read] «فظَلِلْتُمْ» in the original form with two lāms, the first with kasra; fatḥa on it is transmitted from al-Jaḥdarī, and that is also a dialectal form.
The majority [read] «تَفَكَّهون» with hāʾ, meaning: you regret; its literal meaning is: you cast off merriment (al-fukāha) from yourselves, and merriment is only cast off out of disgrace; so it is of the category of «تَحَرَّج», «تَأَثَّم» and «تَحَوَّب». It has also been said: «تَفَكَّهون»: you wonder. It has also been said: you blame one another. It has also been said: you lament; and this is an explanation by what is entailed (bi-l-lāzim).
Abū Ḥarām al-ʿUklī read «تَفَكَّنون» with nūn, like «تَتَنَدَّمون» (you regret). Ibn Khālawayh said: "«تَفَكَّهَ» is to wonder, and «تَفَكَّن» is to regret." In the hadith: «مَثَلُ العالِمِ مَثَلُ الحَمَّة يَأْتيها البُعَداء ويترُكها القُرَباء. فبيناهُمْ إذ غار ماؤها فانتفع بها قومٌ وبقي قومٌ يَتَفَكَّنون» ("The likeness of the scholar is the likeness of a hot spring: those far away come to it and those near leave it; then, while they are thus, its water sinks away; some people had benefited from it, and some people remained regretting"), i.e. regretting.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ}: Abū Bakr read «أإنا» as a question, and he follows his principle of pronouncing both hamzas fully without inserting an alif between them; the rest [read it] as a statement. Before this clause there is an implied «قول» (saying) on both readings, and that is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "you would remain regretting, saying" or "you would say: we are indeed «مُغْرَمون»", i.e. burdened with the loss of what we spent, or destroyed by the destruction of our provision, from al-gharām, which is destruction; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Among [instances of] al-gharām in the sense of destruction is his saying:
4218 - إن يُعَذِّبْ يَكُنْ غَراماً وإنْ يُعْ ... طِ جَزيلاً فإنَّه لا يُبالي (If he punishes, it is destruction; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care [how much].)

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً}: the absence of the lām in the apodosis of this «لو» has been discussed before. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was the lām put into the apodosis of «لو» in His saying {لَجَعَلْنَاهُ حُطَاماً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 65] and removed from it here? I say: since «لو» enters upon two clauses, the second of which is made dependent on the first as the requital is made dependent on the condition, and it does not purely denote condition like «إنْ», nor does it govern as it does, but the meaning of condition merely runs into it incidentally, inasmuch as it conveys concerning the contents of its two clauses that the second was prevented because of the prevention of the first — it needed in its apodosis something set up as a sign of this dependence, so this lām was added to be a sign of that. If it is omitted after it has become a well-known sign of its position, that is because when a thing is known and its position is well known, and it has become familiar and customary, its dropping from the wording is not minded, since the hearer's knowledge suffices. Do you not see what is told of Ruʾba, that he used to say «خير» to someone who asked him 'how did you wake up this morning?' — he omitted the preposition because everyone knew its place, and its presence and omission were equal because the matter was so well known. And sufficient for you is the saying of Aws:
4219 - حتى إذا الكَلاَّبُ قال لها ... كاليومِ مَطْلوباً ولا طَلَبا (Until, when the dog-handler said to it: [never have I seen] a quarry like today's, nor a pursuit.)
He omitted «لم أَرَ» (I have not seen). Its omission is a verbal abbreviation, while it is present in the meaning, so the two positions are equal without any difference between them. Moreover, its having been mentioned before, with the distance short, makes mentioning it a second time unnecessary. It may also be said that this lām undoubtedly conveys the meaning of emphasis, so it was put into the verse about what is eaten and not into the verse about what is drunk, to indicate that the matter of what is eaten comes before the matter of what is drunk, and that the threat of losing it is more severe and harder, in that drink is only needed as a consequence of food. Do you not see that you give your guest to drink only after you have fed him? And if you reversed it, you would fall under the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ:
4220 - إذا سُقِيَتْ ضُيوفُ الناس مَحْضاً ... سَقَوْا أضيافَهم شَبِماً زُلالا (When people's guests are given pure milk to drink, they give their guests cold, clear water to drink.)
And one of the Arabs was given a drink and said: 'I only drink on top of a full belly (thamīla).' For this reason the verse about food was put before the verse about drink." End of quotation.
Al-Shaykh said: "Al-Zamakhsharī has been long-winded", and he did not mention this fine discussion; then he mentioned part of his words, and took him to task over his saying "that the second was prevented because of the prevention of the first", making it the expression of some weak parsers. Then he mentioned Sībawayh's expression, which is: "a particle for what would have happened because of the happening of something else", and mentioned that the saying of whoever said "prevention because of prevention" is invalidated by your saying: "if this were a human being, it would be an animal", i.e. the prevention of humanity does not entail the prevention of animality. Objections like these are easy, and if a man follows people in their expression, there is no blame on him; moreover, it is the expression of the early grammarians, as more than one has stated.
And His saying: {مِنَ المزن}: the clouds; it is a generic noun whose singular is «مُزْنة». The poet said: 4221 - فلا مُزْنَةٌ وَدَقَتْ وَدْقَها ... ولا أرضَ أَبْقَلَ إبْقالَها (No raincloud ever poured down rain like hers, and no land ever brought forth herbage like hers.)
And the other said:
4222 - ونحن كماءِ المُزْنِ ما في نِصابِنا ... كَهامٌ ولا فينا يُعَدُّ بخيلُ (We are like the water of the rainclouds: in our stock there is no dullness, and among us no miser is counted.)

semin-durr:71-71.t: His saying: {تُورُونَ}: from «أَوْرَيْتُ الزَّنْدَ», i.e. you struck the fire-stick and brought out its fire; and «وَرِي الزَّنْدُ يَرِي», i.e. its fire came out. The original of «تُوْرُوْن» is «تُوْرِيُون».

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying: {لِّلْمُقْوِينَ}: one says «أَقْوَى الرجلُ» when he settles in the qiwāʾ land, which is the empty waste, like «أصْحَرَ»: he entered the desert. «أَقْوَتِ الدار»: the abode became empty, from that, because it becomes a waste. Al-Nābigha said:
4223 - يا دارَميَّةَ بالعَلْياءِ فالسَّنَدِ ... أَقْوَتْ وطال عليها سالفُ الأبَدِ (O abode of Mayya on the height, then the hillside: it has become deserted, and long ages have passed over it.)

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ}: the majority read it «فلا», with lām-alif, and there are several views on it. The first: it is a particle of negation, and what is negated by it is omitted, namely the speech of the denying unbeliever, its implied form being: "there is no argument for what the unbeliever says"; then He began an oath by what He mentioned. A group of exegetes and grammarians held this. This has been judged weak because it involves omitting both the noun and the predicate of «لا». Al-Shaykh said: "It is not permissible." It should not [be dismissed thus], for the one who held this is someone like Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, the student of the scholar of the Qurʾān and its ocean, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both; and it is unlikely that Saʿīd would say it except on the basis of received instruction (tawqīf).
The second: it is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, like it in His saying: {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 29], the implied form being "so I swear" and "so that [they] may know"; and like his saying:
4224 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فلا وأَبي أعدائِها لا أَخُوْنُها (… nay, by the father of her enemies, I will not betray her.)
The third: it is the lām of the beginning (lām al-ibtidāʾ), the original being «فَلأُقْسِمُ»; the fatḥa was lengthened and an alif was generated from it, as in his saying:
4225 - أَعوذُ باللَّهِ من العَقْرابِ ... (I seek refuge with Allah from the scorpion.) Al-Shaykh said this, and cited as evidence the reading of Hishām «أَفْئِيْدَة». I say: this is very weak. He also relied on the reading of al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā «فَلأُقْسِمُ» with a single lām. I say: there are two explanations of this reading. The first: the lām is the lām of the beginning, and after it is an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the verb; when the mubtadaʾ was omitted, the lām became joined to its khabar, its implied form being «فلأَنا أٌقْسِمُ» (so indeed I swear), like «لَزيدٌ منطلقٌ»; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Jinnī said this. The second: it is the lām of the oath entering upon a present-tense verb. It is possible for the oath to be the answer to an oath, as in His saying: {وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنَا} [al-Tawba: 107]: «ليَحْلِفُنَّ» itself is an oath whose answer is «إنْ أرَدْنَا», and it is the answer to an implied oath; likewise this. This is the view of the Kufans: they permit swearing upon a present-tense verb. The Basrans reject it and explain what suggests that as involving an implied mubtadaʾ, so that the oath relates to a nominal clause. Al-Zamakhsharī rejected its being the lām of the oath, saying: "For two reasons. The first: it ought to be accompanied by the emphatic nūn, and omitting it is weak and ugly. The second: «لأفعلنَّ» in the answer of an oath is for the future, whereas the verb of the oath must be for the present." This, as mentioned, is because he holds the doctrine of the Basrans. The meaning of his saying "the verb of the oath must be for the present" is that the verb of the oath is a performative (inshāʾ), and the performative is present. As for his saying "that the nūn be joined to it", this is the doctrine of the Basrans; the Kufans permit the lām and the nūn to alternate, as in «واللَّهِ لأَضْرِبُ زيداً» (by Allah, I will strike Zayd), as in his saying:
4226 - لَئِن تَكُ قد ضاقَتْ عليكم بيوتُكمْ ... لَيَعْلَمُ ربِّي أنَّ بيتيَ واسعُ (If your houses have become too narrow for you, my Lord surely knows that my house is wide.)
and «وواللَّهِ اضربَنَّ زيداً», as in his saying: 4227 - وقتيلُ مُرَّةَ أَثْأَرَنَّ. . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (And the one slain by Murra I will surely avenge …)
Something close to this verse has been given at His saying: {فَلاَ وَرَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ حتى يُحَكِّمُوكَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 65]; but there, there is what cannot be said here, just as here there is what cannot be said there. Something close to it will come in al-Qiyāma in the reading of Ibn Kathīr {لأُقْسِمُ بيوم القيامة} [al-Qiyāma: 1].
The majority read «بمواقِع» in the plural, and the two brothers [read] «بموقع» in the singular with a plural meaning, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it was made singular. Their mawāqiʿ are their places of falling and their places of setting.
It has also been said: their falling on the day they are dimmed. It has also been said: the stars [stand] for the Qurʾān [revealed in instalments]; this is supported by «وإنَّه لَقَسَمٌ» and {إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ}. What is sworn upon is His saying: {إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ}; on this view there are two parentheses in the speech. The first: the parenthesis of His saying «وإنه لَقَسَمٌ» between the oath and what is sworn upon. The second: the parenthesis of His saying «لو تعلمون» between the adjective and the described noun. Ibn ʿAṭiyya refused to make His saying «وإنَّه لَقَسَمٌ» a parenthesis, and said: "«وإنه لَقَسَمٌ» is an emphasising of the matter and a drawing of attention to what is sworn by; this is not a parenthesis between the two utterances; rather, it is a meaning intended to be given importance; the parenthesis is only His saying «لو تعلمون»." I say: its being emphasis and drawing attention to the greatness of what is sworn by does not contradict its being parenthetical; rather, this is the meaning of parenthesis and its benefit.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يَمَسُّهُ}: there are two views on this «لا». The first: it is negating, so the ḍamma in «لا يَمَسُّه» is a ḍamma of inflection. On this view there are two views on the clause. The first: its position is genitive as an adjective of «كتاب». What is meant by «كتاب» is either the Preserved Tablet, the purified ones then being the angels; or what is meant by it is the written copies (maṣāḥif), and what is meant by the purified ones is all those legally responsible (mukallafūn). The second: its position is nominative as an adjective of «قرآن», and what is meant by the purified ones is the angels only, i.e. none has access to it, or none touches its tablet. One of these two loose usages is necessary, because attributing touching to meanings literally is impossible. Its being a negation is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «ما يَمَسُّه» with the negating «ما».
The second of the two original views: it is prohibitive (nāhiya), and the verb after it is jussive (majzūm); had it been released from assimilation (idghām), that would have appeared in it, as in His saying: {لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سوء} [Āl ʿImrān: 174]; but it was assimilated, and when it was assimilated its final letter was given ḍamma because of the hāʾ of the absent masculine pronoun; Sībawayh knew nothing but the ḍamma in cases like this. In the hadith: «إنَّا لم نَرُدُّه عليك إلاَّ أننا حُرُمٌ» ("We only returned it to you because we are in the state of iḥrām"), although analogy requires that fatḥa also be permissible for lightness. By what I have mentioned, the invalidity of the objection of whoever objected that, had this been a prohibition, one would say «لا يَمَسَّه» with fatḥa, becomes clear; for the permissibility of ḍamma on what precedes the hāʾ in this kind was hidden from him, especially on the view of Sībawayh, who permits nothing else. Ibn ʿAṭiyya judged its being a prohibition weak, [saying]: "If it is a statement, it is in the position of an adjective, and His saying after that «تنْزيلٌ» is an adjective; so if we make it a prohibition, it is something foreign interposed between the adjectives, and that is not good in the arrangement of speech; so reflect on it. In the reading (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd: «ما يمسُّه»." End of quotation.
There is no weakening of this view in what he mentioned, because we do not concede that «تنزيل» is an adjective; rather, it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a revelation", so the interposition he mentioned does not follow. And even if we concede that it is an adjective, then «لا يَمَسُّه» is also an adjective; and if it is objected against us that it is a request [and requests cannot be adjectives], the answer is that it is on an implied «قول» (saying), i.e. "about which it is said: let none touch it", as they said about His saying «فتنةً لا تصيبَنَّ» on the view that «لا تصيبنَّ» is a prohibition; and it is like his saying:
4228 - جاؤوا بمَذْقٍ هل رأيْتَ الذئبَ قطّ ... (They brought watered-down milk [of a colour of which one would say]: have you ever seen the wolf?) Its verification has been given in al-Anfāl. To this question is connected the scholars' disagreement about one in a state of ritual impurity touching the muṣḥaf, and it is built upon this; its verification will come more fully than this in the book "Aḥkām al-Qurʾān", if Allah the Exalted wills its completion.
The majority read «المُطَهَّرون» with the ṭāʾ light and the hāʾ doubled with fatḥa, as a passive participle. From Salmān al-Fārisī likewise, except with kasra on the hāʾ, as an active participle, i.e. those who purify themselves, its object having been omitted. Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr in a transmission from them, and ʿĪsā, [read] with sukūn on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the light hāʾ, a passive participle from «أطهر». Zayd, al-Ḥasan, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn and also Salmān [read] «المُطَّهِّرُوْن» with the ṭāʾ doubled and the hāʾ [doubled] with kasra; its original is «المتطهِّرون», which was assimilated. It has also been read in this original form.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
It has also been read «تنزيلاً» in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun; that is permissible because it is specified by the adjective. Or it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) of an implied governor, i.e. "it was sent down a sending-down"; and «التنزيل» became predominantly applied to the Qurʾān.
«من رَبِّ» may be attached to it on the first view, not the second, because the emphasising [maṣdar] does not govern; so [on the second] it is attached to an omitted word, being an adjective of it. As for the reading «تنزيل» in the nominative, both views are permissible.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {أفبهذا}: attached to the khabar (predicate); its being placed before the mubtadaʾ (subject) is permissible because that is permissible for its governor. The underlying form is: "are you then «مُدْهِنون» regarding this discourse?", which is the Qurʾān. The meaning of «مُدْهِنون» is: treating lightly, like one who is accommodating (yudhinu) in a matter, i.e. who softens his side and is not firm in it, treating it lightly. One says «أَدْهَن فلانٌ», i.e. he was soft and compromising in what should not be borne [by the one compromised with]. [Translator's note: «فيما لا يُحْمَلُ عند المُدْهَنِ» is obscure; rendered approximately.] The poet said:
4229 - الحَزْمُ والقُوَّةُ خيرٌ من الْ ... إدْهانِ والفَهَّةِ والهاعِ (Resolve and strength are better than compromise, feeble-wittedness and faint-heartedness.)
Al-Rāghib said: "Al-idhān originally is like al-tadhīn (anointing with oil), but it was made an expression for cajoling, being soft and abandoning seriousness, just as al-taqrīd, which is removing ticks, was made an expression for that."

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying: {وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is by way of mocking them, because they put the thing in other than its place, as in your saying «شَتَمني حيث أَحْسَنْتُ إليه» (he reviled me when I did him good), i.e. he reversed the case of kindness. From this is:
4230 - كأن شُكْرَ القَوْمِ عند المِنَنِ ... كيُّ الصَحيحاتِ وفَقْءُ الأعينِ (As if the people's thanks for favours were the branding of healthy [camels] and the gouging out of eyes.)
i.e. [you make] the thanks for your provision your denial. The second: there are two omitted muḍāfs (first terms of annexation), i.e. "in place of thanks for your provision", so that the meaning is sound; Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik said this; more than this has been given to you at His saying: {فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ} [al-Najm: 9]. The third: al-rizq is thanks in the dialect of Azd Shanūʾa: «ما رَزَقَ فلانٌ فلاناً», i.e. he did not thank him; so on this view there is no omission at all. This is supported by the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and his student ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them, «وتَجْعَلون شُكْرَكم» in place of «رِزْقَكم».
The majority read «تُكَذِّبون», from al-takdhīb (denying). ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal from him, [read] «تَكْذِبون», light, from al-kadhib (lying).

semin-durr:83-83.t: His saying: {فَلَوْلاَ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الحلقوم}: the order of the noble verse is: "why then do you not bring it back — i.e. the soul — when it reaches the throat, if you are not «مَدِيْنين»?" The second «فلولا» is repeated for emphasis; al-Zamakhsharī said this. I say: so the implied form is "why then, why then do you not bring it back", of the category of verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī), and «إذا بَلَغَت» is an adverb of «تَرْجِعونها» placed before it, since nothing prevents that, i.e. why do you not bring back the soul at the time of its reaching the throat? And His saying: {وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the agent of «بَلَغَتْ». The tanwīn in «حينئذٍ» is a substitute for the clause to which «إذا» is annexed, i.e. "when it reaches the throat" — contrary to al-Akhfash, who claimed that the tanwīn is that of full declension (ṣarf) and the kasra is for inflection; its verification has been given before.

semin-durr:84-84.t: The majority read «حينئذٍ» with fatḥa on the nūn, because it is accusative as an adverb, what puts it in the accusative being «تَنْظُرون». ʿĪsā [read] it with kasra; it is problematic and not far from being an error on his part. It has been explained as assimilation (itbāʿ) to the vowel of the hamza, and there is nothing strange in that, for it is no more far-fetched than the reading «الحمدِ للَّهِ» [al-Fātiḥa: 1] with kasra on the dāl, because of the two annexed words being inseparable and because of their especially frequent use.

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. you look on in this state which is hidden from you; or it may be resumptive and thus parenthetical; and the restriction [«ولكن لا تُبصرون»] is clear. The seeing (al-baṣar) may be from insight (al-baṣīra) or from eyesight, i.e. you do not see the helpers of the Angel of Death.

semin-durr:86-86.t:
And {إِن كُنتُمْ}: a condition whose apodosis is omitted according to the Basrans, because «فلولا» indicates it, or placed before it according to those who hold that, as has been explained. Al-ḥulqūm is the passage of food. «مَدِيْنين», i.e. governed, or brought to account, or requited; this has been given at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa, praise be to Allah. This is what is summed up concerning the noble verse, set out precisely. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«وتَرْجِعونها» is the apodosis of the first «لولا», and that dispenses with an apodosis of the second. It has also been said: the reverse of that. It has also been said: the second «لولا» is a repetition." End of quotation. Calling the like of this an apodosis is not correct at all, because this is the «لولا» of urging (taḥḍīḍ), which has no apodosis; the apodosis belongs only to the «لولا» of prevention due to existence, as in: {وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 83].
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His saying «تَرْجِعونها» stands in place of the apodoses and the statements that the urgings require, and of «إذا» in His saying «فلولا إذا», and of the repeated «إنْ»; and part of the speech carries another part, by way of concision and abridgement." End of quotation. So he made «إذا» conditional. By his saying "the apodoses" he means [the apodoses] of «إذا», of «إنْ» and of «إنْ» in His saying: {إِن كُنتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ} and {إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ}; and by "the statements" he means the verbs He urged them to. It is an awkward expression, and for that reason I have explained it.
Al-Shaykh said: "«إذا» is not a condition, but an adverb governed by an omitted «تَرْجعونها» after «لولا», because «تَرْجِعونها» in the second urging indicates it. So the first urging came restricted to the time of [the soul's] reaching the throat, and the second urging came made dependent on the negation of their being subject to a lord, while they are unable to bring it back, since their being subject to a lord exists; so they are subdued, with no power." End of quotation. So he made the mentioned «تَرْجِعونها» belong to the second «لولا», indicating an omitted one after the first; this is one of the views Abū al-Baqāʾ reported, mentioned above.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying: {إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ}: another condition. This is not a case of a condition intervening upon a condition, as in «إنْ ركبتِ إنْ لَبِسْتِ فأنتِ طالق» ("if you ride, if you dress, you are divorced"), such that what I said earlier about that question would apply to it; because what is meant here is: if the two conditions exist, however they may be, then why do you not bring back the soul of the dead person?
His saying: {فَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ}: the discussion of «أمَّا» has been given in full at the beginning of this work, praise be to Allah. Here there is an additional matter, namely the occurrence of another condition after it. The grammarians disagreed about the apodosis mentioned after it: does it belong to «أمَّا» or to «إنْ», the apodosis of the other being omitted because what is pronounced indicates it, or is the apodosis for both together? Three views: the first is Sībawayh's; the second is al-Fārisī's in one of his two views — he has another view like Sībawayh's; and the third is al-Akhfash's. This is as was said about the apodosis after two successive conditions. Makkī said: "The meaning of «أمَّا» according to Abū Isḥāq is moving from one thing to another, i.e. leave what we were on and take up something else." I say: on this view the apodosis belongs to «إنْ» only, because «أمَّا» is not a condition. Some preferred that the apodosis belongs to «أمَّا», because the apodosis of «إنْ» is often omitted when it stands alone, so claiming that when it is with another condition is more fitting. The pronoun in «كان» and «كان» refers to the one who dies, as indicated by His saying «فلولا تَرْجِعُونَها».

semin-durr:89-89.t:
Al-rawḥ is rest; this has been given in Yūsuf. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾisha, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda among a large group read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and it is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Ḥasan said: al-rūḥ is mercy, because it is like life for the one shown mercy. From him also: his spirit (rūḥ) goes out in fragrance. The discussion of {رَيْحَانٌ}, the disagreement about it, and the manner of its morphology have been given in the preceding sūra.
And [His saying]: {فَرَوْحٌ} is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is implied before it, i.e. "he shall have rest". It may also be implied after it, because it rests upon the fāʾ of requital.

semin-durr:91-91.t: His saying: {فَسَلاَمٌ لَّكَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). As for «مِنْ أصحاب», al-Zamakhsharī said: "Peace be to you, O companion of the right, from your brothers, the companions of the right, i.e. they greet you with peace." Ibn Jarīr said: "Its meaning is: peace be to you, you being of the companions [of the right]." This may be like al-Zamakhsharī's saying, «أنت» being a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf in «لك»; or he may have meant that «أنت» is a mubtadaʾ and «من أصحابِ» its khabar. This is supported by what some reported, that the meaning is: "it will be said to them: peace be to you; you are of the companions of the right." The first of these views is the clear and evident one; for that reason Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] gave no attention to any other.

semin-durr:94-94.t: His saying: {وَتَصْلِيَةُ}: conjoined to «فنُزُل», i.e. "he shall have hospitality and a roasting". Abū ʿAmr in the transmission of al-Luʾluʾī from him, Aḥmad ibn Mūsā and al-Minqarī read it with the tāʾ in the genitive, conjoined to «مِنْ حميمٍ».

semin-durr:95-95.t: His saying: {حَقُّ اليقين}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a case of annexing the described noun to its adjective. The second: it is of the category of annexing two synonyms by way of intensification, made easier by the difference of their wording. If they have done that with a single word, saying «صوابُ الصوابِ» (the right of the right) and «نفس النفس» (the self of the self) for intensification, then their doing it when the wording differs is all the more fitting.

semin-durr:96-96.t:
His saying: {باسم رَبِّكَ}: the bāʾ may be for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "glorify, accompanied by the name of your Lord", by way of seeking blessing, as in His saying: {وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ} [al-Baqara: 30]. Or it may be for transitivity, on the view that «سَبَّح» is sometimes transitive by itself, as in His saying: {سَبِّحِ اسم رَبِّكَ} [al-Aʿlā: 1], and sometimes by a preposition, as in this verse; claiming that it is redundant goes against the basic rule.
And «العظيم» may be an adjective of «الاسم», or of «ربك», since each of them is genitive. Each of them has been described [elsewhere], in His saying: «تَبَارَكَ اسم رَبِّكَ ذُو الجلال» [al-Raḥmān: 78] and {ذي الجلال}. Because the two annexed words differ in inflection [there], the difference in the description became apparent.
